intent: Changed: widened the sensor row from a 0.016 m to a 0.024 m half-span (5 sensors at 12 mm spacing, y = 0.04 m), following the Integrator's first requested change. Kept sensor_size, wheel track, wheel radius, body and mass so the race isolates the row effect. Expected result: later first departure from the line and higher progress on all three tracks, with a possible first completion on the oval. If progress still stalls near 0.1 to 0.2 with off-track endings, the next candidate is lower yaw inertia (wheel_track 0.10 m or mass 0.6 kg), which I am considering but have not committed to.
learning: Compare against iteration 0: if progress rises on all three tracks, the row was the limiting factor and the widened row should be kept. If the robot still leaves early with max_error near 0.06 m and no saturation, the limit is more likely yaw response or speed, so I will test lower yaw inertia next. Check whether line_loss_events cluster on the slalom, since that track is the weakest.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced the symmetric five-sensor baseline and every trial on every track ended off_track, with no completions. Progress was only 0.176 on the oval, 0.135 on the s-bend and 0.094 on the slalom, so the robot leaves the line early, before the course is half done. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06 m for this body, and widening the body does not raise it above 0.06 m until body_width is near 0.19 m, so body width is not a useful lever. The sensor row is the main geometry lever. With 12 mm sensors at x = -0.016 to +0.016, the outermost footprint reaches only about 0.022 m from the centre line, so once the robot drifts toward the edge of the tape the outer sensors read background and the signal has little headroom to correct. Feedback from the Integrator was design reasoning only, with no Integrator race evidence yet. It set the trigger for widening: saturation or dropout on tight bends. The race shows early departure from the line, which is consistent with that trigger, though I do not have per-step telemetry to confirm saturation directly. I am therefore taking the Integrator's first suggested change: widen the row to a 0.024 m half-span at the same 12 mm sensor size and 0.04 m forward position. I am keeping wheel_track, mass and body unchanged so that the race isolates the effect of the row. I expect more progress before the first off-track event, and possibly completion on the oval, but the slalom may still fail.
